result.title: When Rewards Depend on the Group, GRPO Plays a Tournament
result.summary: Rewards for diversity, coverage and distribution matching make the reward of each sampled response depend on the rest of its group, and they are now routinely optimized with GRPO and RLOO. We prove that in this setting the group-relative baseline changes the objective. The expected update equals each response's own reward gradient plus $α$ times its effect on its groupmates' rewards, with $α=-1/(K-1)$ for groups of size $K$, so GRPO trains every response to beat its groupmates in a zero-sum tournament. It cannot see a pairwise diversity bonus when K=2, sees less than half of it at any K, and often does worse than using no baseline at all. Setting $α=+1$ gives Team-GRPO, an unbiased estimator for any group-dependent reward that works with two samples per prompt and requires no extra model calls for pairwise rewards. The theory predicts training quantitatively. It locates the fixed points of a 9B policy to within 0.02 in $\ell_1$ and predicts how concentrated trained policies become with Pearson r=0.995. On GlobalOpinionQA, GRPO collapses onto the majority answer and ends further from human opinion than the untrained model, while Team-GRPO cuts the error from $0.20$ to $0.08$. On NoveltyBench, Team-GRPO avoids the diversity collapse of GRPO and significantly improves set utility.

AI.brief_summary: 论文证明当奖励依赖同组其他回答时，GRPO/RLOO 的组相对基线会改变优化目标，引入系数为 -1/(K-1) 的组内零和竞争项，并提出取 α=+1 的无偏估计器 Team-GRPO，在多样性、覆盖度类奖励上验证了理论预测与训练收益。
AI.relevance_reason: 纯文本 RL 方法，但为可供核查的线索：若 LVR 训练使用多样性、覆盖度或集合效用的组依赖奖励，组内基线偏置可能影响对 latent 轨迹的信用分配并加剧多样性坍缩。
